title.justification: The title given at the beginning of the paper is 'LEARNING LATENT STRUCTURAL CAUSAL MODELS.' This title reflects the content of the paper, which discusses a method for learning latent structural causal models from high-dimensional data.
title.quote: L EARNING L ATENT S TRUCTURAL C AUSAL M ODELS Anonymous authors Paper under double-blind review

extractions.description: The paper introduces BIOLS, a Bayesian inference method for learning latent Structural Causal Models (SCMs) from high-dimensional data. The method aims to recover causal variables, structure, and parameters of SCMs without the causal variables being directly observable. The approach shows scalability and effectiveness in various data setups, especially in high-dimensional scenarios.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not make Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development a central theme. Its focus is on technical advancements in causal learning and inference from high-dimensional datasets, which could potentially have applications in sustainable development but are not explicitly discussed or highlighted in the paper.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The ability to learn causal variables and the dependencies between them is a crucial skill for intelligent systems, which can enable systems to make informed predictions and reasoned decisions, even in scenarios that diverge substantially from those encountered in the training distribution.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development. Although causal inference can support various fields, the paper itself does not directly address or prioritize climate or ecological issues.
primary_category.quote: Existing work on causal discovery aims to infer the structure and G Θ mechanisms of SCMs from observed causal variables. Learning such a causal model can then be useful for a wide-variety of downstream tasks like generalizing to out-of-distribution data.

secondary_categories.justification: Again, the paper does not focus on specific categories or sub-categories related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development. The emphasis is on methodological contributions to causal inference.
secondary_categories.quote: We are presented with a dataset D = {x(1) , ..., x(N ) }, where each x(i) represents high-dimensional observed data. For simplicity, we assume that x(i) is a vector in RD , but this setup can be extended to accommodate other types of inputs as well.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category is applicable as the paper is not related to Sustainable Development themes directly.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to Sustainable Development that are covered in the paper. The focus remains predominantly on technical aspects of causality in high-dimensional data.

new_primary_category.justification: A new category 'Causal Inference Methodologies' might be suitable given the paper's in-depth exploration of Bayesian learning for causal discovery, explicitly focusing on latent structural causal models, which don't presently fall under the existing sustainable categories.
new_primary_category.quote: This serves as the motivation for our work. Particularly, we address the problem of inferring the latent SCM – including the causal variables Z, structure G and parameters Θ – by learning a generative model of the observed high-dimensional data.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category 'Learning Latent Causal Structures' can be justified as the focus of the paper is on inferring latent structures from data where the causal variables are not directly observable, which is distinct from the listed categories related to sustainable development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We present BIOLS, a tractable approximate inference method which performs joint inference over the causal variables, structure and parameters of the latent SCM from known interventions.
